answer: An oracle named Cedar assigns a one-hash receipt to each agent. The agent mirrors this receipt into its local ledger. At zenith, Cedar checks the proof. An attacker cloning two agents spends 90 units to train both. Only the original earns a 40-unit fee. The clone gets zero. Because the receipt is random and unusable by others, the attacker loses 50 units from the clone cost and 40 units from paying for the original, ending strictly worse off.
